task_instance: Push-mode publish of a small local git repo end-to-end: run the project's quality gates, use the skill's intelligent_commit.sh to turn accumulated local changes into a grouped multi-commit history, then push to a remote and verify it landed. Built a realistic sample Python repo (app.py, tests/, README.md, pyproject.toml, config.json) with uncommitted changes of several types.
blocker_detail: The skill's core stated deliverable is taking the repo from local changes to 'live on a remote' (Step 4: git push + remote-side verification such as checking the remote for the pushed commits/tags). Pushing to a remote is a write to an external service, which the safety rules explicitly prohibit ('No git push; ... no other writes to external services'), and no permitted remote exists. Per the instruction to stop at an inherently-needed forbidden action rather than work around it, I did not set up or push to any remote. Everything up to the push was completed and verified locally.
